provenance.dataset: Eye on Methane / MARS detected sources and plumes
provenance.attribution: Contains data from UNEP IMEO Eye on Methane / MARS, licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Changes: normalized the source and plume CSV tables into JSON; source feedback remains source-level; unresolved plume links are retained; no mitigation confirmation is inferred.

sourceLimitations: Priority is an uncalibrated investigation aid, not a physical leak likelihood or future-flux forecast.
The calibrated recurrence estimate predicts another linked MARS archive record within 365 days for a source already observed; it does not predict methane presence, emissions, repair, or mitigation.
The observed flux trend summarizes discrete detection dates only; it is not extrapolated and is not a future forecast.
A descriptive trend is emitted only with four or more numeric dates spanning at least 90 days; the method summarizes dated flux with a median pairwise Theil–Sen slope.
Observation coverage varies by sensor, revisit schedule, geography, and cloud conditions; missing observations do not mean zero emissions.
Source notification and feedback metadata do not verify recipient, repair, or emissions reduction.
This small curated casebook has not been independently validated as a predictive model.

nextChecks.title: Obtain the dated action record
nextChecks.acceptance: Identify the facility/source, action, responsible party, action date and inspectable attributable reference within the selected period.

nextChecks.title: Obtain the follow-up measurement and method
nextChecks.acceptance: Provide an attributable follow-up dated on or after the action and within the scope, measurement method, observation opportunities, units and uncertainty. Same-day records require finer timing before inferring an order. Missing detections are not zero emissions.

nextChecks.title: Inspect contents and record the human decision
nextChecks.acceptance: Check authenticity, attribution, exact citations and document rights. Save an authorized human assessment separately from this metadata-coverage analysis.

limitations: Reference eligibility and sensitivity are decision support, not document authentication or physical mitigation verification.
Removing a reference tests decision dependence; it is not a probability, uncertainty estimate, or forecast.
The digest is an unsigned checksum. Independently check the publisher snapshot and a trusted commitment before inferring authenticity.
Same-day action and follow-up dates meet the metadata rule but do not establish the order of physical events.
